title: Grateful Dead Live at Public Hall on 1973-12-06

ai_review.summary: High‑quality soundboard capture of a historic ’73 show with an epic Here Comes Sunshine and a divisive, marathon Dark Star.
ai_review.review: The Miller SBD upgrade delivers clear, well‑balanced audio that lets the band’s 1973 magic shine through.  Listeners rave about the 20‑minute Here Comes Sunshine, the sprawling Dark Star/Eyes/Stella sequence, and a powerhouse Big River, while noting a few minor cuts (the first 20 seconds of Dark Star) and a thin Bobby guitar mix later in the set.  Overall the performance is hailed as a top‑tier Dead show despite some uneven moments in the first set.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 5‑star praise for both performance and sound; a few note minor audio gaps but they do not detract from the overall excellence of the show.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Upgrade is noticeably clearer than earlier versions; crisp mix with solid instrument separation. Minor issues: first ~20 s of Dark Star missing and a faint Bobby guitar in later jams, but no major drop‑outs.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
poor_songs: Beat It On Down the Line
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is solid but a bit uneven, with highlights like Bertha and China>Rider; second set erupts into a legendary Here Comes Sunshine and an exploratory Dark Star that defines the night.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar tone and vocal delivery are repeatedly praised—especially on Here Comes Sunshine, Dark Star, and Big River.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesch’s bass is described as “smoldering,” “fuzz‑tone,” and echo‑laden; several reviewers liken his early‑70s sound to jazz bassist Miroslav Vitouš.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s rhythm guitar and on‑stage banter receive positive nods; his vocals stand out on Ramble on Rose and Me & My Uncle.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux gets kudos for warm piano on Big River and a tasteful switch to Rhodes during Dark Star.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming is called “drum‑kit to death” on Big River, providing relentless drive throughout the marathon jams.
